Team: Pin-Yun Kuo (A), Bo Wu (B), Rushabh Mutha (C), Zongyan Yang (D)
Date: 20 Nov 2026 · Ref: ADRs 001–003, Compose Verified
Executive Summary: LAME is a containerized spot exchange that strictly isolates a deterministic, strongly consistent core trading path (A → D → B) from an asynchronous generative AI Market Analyst (Service C, Ollama RAG) and unified cluster observability (Prometheus :9090, Grafana :3001, React Admin /dashboard). Live compose fault injection confirms 0 ledger deviations across 253 orders while stopping C or Ollama adds 0 ms to matching.
01 Requirements, Load-Bearing Constraints & Scope Boundaries

Four Load-Bearing Architectural Constraints

  • Zero Spot Overdraft & Finality: Ledger holds enforce CHECK (available ≥ 0); matched trades on B cannot be reversed without breaking price-time priority, so risk must gate before B and holds never release on timeout.
  • Determinism vs. Probabilistic AI: B (events-<day>.db) and D (d.db) demand bitwise crash replay; C's LLM calls take 0.4–3.0+ s and process untrusted text.
  • Graceful Degradation: A → D → B fails closed on D outage and sheds load on tail spikes, while C/Ollama stalls never degrade trading.
  • Full Observability: All 4 services expose Prometheus /metrics covering RPS, ≥500 server errors, latency percentiles, and AI token spend.

Scope, Pair Grid & Explicit Non-Goals

In Scope: Two live pairs (BTC-USDT, ETH-USDT; 6 quantity decimals, USDT 6 decimals) with limit, market, cancel, and quantity-only modify orders settled against Postgres holds; scripted & multi-market news replay via RabbitMQ; deterministic pre-trade R1/R2 checks; offline single-command startup via docker compose up --build.

Out of Scope: Real fiat deposits/withdrawals, margin/leverage (deferred stretch), external exchange routing, and AI-driven trade execution or investment advice.

04 Trade-Off Analysis (Week 2 & Week 10 Three-Step Method · ~1 Page)

Applying Entangled Dimensions → Coupling Points → Concrete Scenarios (without invented weights), naming three specific downsides per chosen option:

1. Hold vs. Optimistic Release (ADR-002)

Conflict: Fund liquidity vs. zero-overdraft ledger invariant (CHECK ≥ 0) across A's Postgres lock and D/B's async notification boundary.

Scenario: Releasing after A's 2 s HTTP timeout restores cash quickly, yet a fill already in B settles against re-spent funds and halts settlement globally. Holding until D's notification freezes only the funds of orders already in flight while D is down; new orders are refused before anything is held. With D killed for ~49 s on 20 Nov, A accepted again 1.2 s after D was ready, and an 8 s pause turned the in-flight order into a cancel whose hold returned 1.2 s after D came back.

Made worse: (1) "Confirming" UX friction, (2) in-flight balance freezes during D/B restarts, (3) extra reconciliation states/tests.

2. Fail-Closed R1+R2 Gate vs. Async/R1 (ADR-001)

Conflict: Manipulation integrity & bitwise replay vs. availability & latency on B's single /d channel.

Scenario: Post-trade checks remove gate latency but cannot unwind matched wash fills. Dropping R2 during bursts keeps single-user checks up (and B still enforces in-matcher self-trade prevention) while exposing cross-account wash rings exactly during traffic floods. D achieves 2 ms decision p99 (7 ms 202 p99 w/ real B in Compose), while A sheds safely.

Made worse: (1) total order/cancel halt when D stops, (2) conservative linked-account false positives, (3) extra synchronous hop.

3. Off-Path FTS5 AI vs. Embedded RAG (ADR-003)

Conflict: Single-container simplicity & zero staleness vs. latency isolation, replay safety, & trust containment.

Scenario: Running Ollama RAG inside A couples 3 s inference stalls and untrusted prompt inputs onto balance-hold worker threads. Vector embeddings add VRAM/latency drift vs. deterministic FTS5 BM25 inside one atomic news_c.db.

Made worse: (1) up to 3 s market-snapshot lag + news replay delay, (2) larger multi-container footprint (RabbitMQ + Ollama), (3) duplicated ticker normalization.

05 AI Components & Architectural Implications (Week 7, 8 & 10 Framework)

Trust Boundary, Determinism & Brownout Protection

  • Autonomy vs. Safety (Tenancy/Trust Cluster): Untrusted news and user prompts run through 3 rails: regex pre-screening blocks injection overrides and financial advice pre-LLM (REJECTED_UNSAFE), embedded injections are stripped on ingest (sanitized), retrieved docs sit inside <retrieved_evidence> XML tags, and post-LLM citation verification checks whether cited IDs exist in FTS5's retrieved set and strips unretrieved IDs.
  • Determinism vs. Creativity (Change Cluster): Pins temperature = 0.0, enforces LLMStructuredOutput JSON Schema, tags every answer with FTS5 index_version, and refuses cleanly via BM25 evidence gating (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE).

Slow > Dead, Invalidation & Token Spend Economics

  • Accuracy vs. Latency (Failure & Invalidation): C sits off-path (0 ms trading tax) and enforces a 3.0 s socket timeout on Ollama HTTP calls, returning HTTP 503 or deterministic synthesis fallback (22.59 ms / 14.65 ms in F1). Surfaces data_freshness_seconds & source (noting /api/activity and fallback seeds also populate cache alongside service_b_ws).
  • Spend Is Load (Cost Cluster): Safety and BM25 refusal gates short-circuit before calling Ollama — saving 4,900 tokens in the 20 Nov compose run at $0.00 local spend vs hosted reference ($0.10 / $0.30 per 1M). Note: tokens_saved_by_gates (total_refusals * 350) also counts post-inference sufficient_evidence=false refusals.
06 Cost, Deployment & Unified Observability Architecture

Root docker-compose.yml launches the full cluster via one command (docker compose up --build) with isolated per-quantum volumes (service_a_pgdata, service_b_data, service_d_data, service_c_data, ollama_models, prometheus_data, grafana_data). Running llama3.2:1b locally avoids cloud token bills inside ~2 GB Ollama RAM + 512 MB capped for Rust service-b. Scaling bottleneck identified: A applies D's notifications one transaction at a time (18–31 ms), capping settlement at ~10–15 trades/s on a laptop; contiguous batch commit resolves this cleanly.

Observability Split & Hardening: Grafana (:3001) queries Prometheus (5 s scrapes), whereas React Admin /dashboard fetches metrics directly from Service C's /api/observability aggregator (which polls A/B/D /metrics with isolated per-target timeouts). Errors count strictly HTTP ≥ 500 (4xx tracked as client_4xx), D rejections match decision="REJECTED", B tracks OrderEvent outputs (not Trade), and B's displayed p50/p95/p99 in /api/observability all reflect the same startup replay duration (lame_b_replay_duration_seconds).
